I1.quote: we introduce a micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) vacuum sensor in the experiment which is used to measure pressures during the H2 storage in CNTs, and the H2 adsorption capacity could be calculated from the pressure changes.

I2.quote: Sample 1 contains MWNTs of about 60 wt%, which are 0.5–2 μm in length and 10–25 nm in diameter. Others are carbon nanoparticles and amorphous carbon.

I3.quote: At ambient pressure (5.2 × 10^4–1.4 × 10^5 Pa) and room temperature, H2 storage experiments were carried out ... At a pressure of 0.52 atm ... sample 1 stored 0.21 wt% of H2.
I3.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 498), Section 2 Experiment and Section 3 Results; Fig. 3 (p. 3) caption "at room temperature", pressure axis in 10^4 Pa; Fig. 4 (p. 3) temperature axis shows room temperature at about 300 K

I4.quote: Searched text, figures and captions for a specific surface area (BET, Langmuir, m2/g) of samples 1-3; none found. Only a generic remark that CNTs have "large specific surface area" (Introduction) and uptake per film area (g/cm2).

I5.quote: At room temperature and ambient pressure we studied the H2 storage in carbon nanotubes (CNTs) and precisely measured the H2 storage capacity with a sensitive sensor.

notes: Constant-volume pressure-drop measurement (49.30 ml brass cell, blank-cell correction) at room temperature and 0.52-1.4 x 10^5 Pa; sample 1 (arc-discharge MWNT powder, 169.5 mg) 0.26, 0.21 and 0.22 wt%; CVD film sample 2 8.0 wt%; sample 3 per-area only. No specific surface area for any sample, so I4 fails. I3 judged met: temperature is stated in words ("room temperature") and is recoverable as about 300 K from the Fig. 4 axis for sample 1 in the same cell; pressures are stated and readable from Fig. 2/3 axes. If an adjudicator holds that "room temperature" alone does not satisfy I3, the first code becomes no_conditions_stated; the paper is ineligible either way.
